- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first few days, then gradually flatten — true prices often dip sharply after initial spikes.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and stay high longer than actual price reverts.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the medium term — true prices often return to lower levels after peaks.
- Forecasts are too smooth; true price movements show more volatility and sharper transitions, especially in the second half of the 30-day window.
- Model underreacts to recent price drops — when true prices fall sharply, forecasts remain stubbornly high.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (first 5–10 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (last 10–20 days).
